key_insight: Multimodal Flow proposes a single, fully continuous generative framework for both language and vision in shared embedding spaces. This removes the need to mix discrete text prediction with quantized or modality-specific image generation.
problem_solved: Existing unified multimodal models often rely on discrete tokens for both modalities or use separate objectives/sampling for text and images. This creates a visual quantization bottleneck and makes multimodal generation less consistent and harder to unify.
method: Model language and vision with a shared continuous flow-based generative process in embedding space.
Avoid image quantization and modality-specific decoding by learning a unified representation for both modalities.
Use a single sampling/generation mechanism across language and vision to simplify multimodal generation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could simplify multimodal model design by reducing modality-specific components and avoiding quantization loss in images. It also points toward more coherent and flexible joint generation of text and visual content.

paper_title: Multimodal Flow: Unified Flow Modeling of Language and Vision in Embedding Spaces
